description: Use NASA Earth data to help farmers identify suitable crop rotations, improve soil health, and adapt to changing climate and water conditions.
summary:
A decision-support dashboard built to help farmers under the the Challenge: Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data. 
Farmers in Oman, Al Batinah North face extreme heat, coastal soil salinity and scarce water, yet lack field-level guidance on what to plant and how much to irrigate. AgriQuantum is a decision-support dashboard that turns NASA data into clear actions for each field. It pulls live NASA POWER weather, counts days at or above 40 °C and 45 °C, and calculates evaporation demand (ET₀) using the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method. Salinity is estimated from distance to the coast and shown only as Low, Medium or High. For each of three pilot fields, farmers see a 0–100 risk score with adjustable weights, a 12-month calendar of when soil sits bare, crop rotation rankings that respond to their priorities, and crop-specific irrigation guidance. Planned layers include HLS, SMAP, GPM IMERG, ECOSTRESS and GRACE-FO. The project is transparent about its limits and calls for local review before farm decisions.
details: AgriQuantum is a web dashboard for three pilot fields in Al Batinah North, Oman, that turns NASA data into clear farm decisions. It pulls live NASA POWER weather (temperature, humidity, wind, solar radiation and rainfall) for the last 400 days, counts heat days at or above 40 °C and 45 °C, and calculates evaporation demand (ET₀) with the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith equation. Salinity is estimated from distance to the coast and shown only as Low, Medium or High. For each field, farmers get a 0–100 risk score, a 12-month bare-soil calendar, crop rotation rankings that update with their priorities, and irrigation guidance by crop, growth stage and method. This helps cut water waste and crop stress, and it helps specialists decide which fields need attention first. The intended impact is stronger farm resilience and water management in water-scarce regions, starting with Oman and later expanding to other arid areas. It runs in the browser, is hosted on Netlify and calls the NASA POWER API, with no special hardware needed. It is creative because it combines regional monitoring with farm-level irrigation guidance and lets each farmer set their own priorities. It also states its uncertainty openly, showing salinity only as a class and labeling placeholder values. The team considered data limits (one 50 km POWER grid cell covers all three fields, and POWER data arrives a few days late), the team's own risk weights, local research, simplicity for farmers, and the need for local review before any farm decision.
